binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω equipped with the structure asserting that it is a probability measure.
X: Ω→ℝ is an arbitrary real-valued function.
K∈ℝ is an arbitrary real constant.
λ∈ℝ is arbitrary after the hypotheses on Ω, μ, X, and K have been fixed.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Ω to the Borel real line.
X is μ-integrable and has mean zero: ∫Ω X(ω) dμ(ω)=0.
X is bounded in absolute value by K μ-almost everywhere: |X(ω)|≤K for μ-almost every ω.
conclusions: Its integral satisfies ∫Ω exp(λX(ω)) dμ(ω) ≤ exp(((λ²/2)/(1-|λ|K/3))·∫Ω X(ω)² dμ(ω)).
mathematical_definitions: Because μ is a probability measure, the integrals may be read as expectations: Eμ[X]=0, Eμ[e^{λX}] is the moment-generating expression, and ∫X²dμ=Eμ[X²].
The scalar multiplying the second moment is (λ²/2)/(1-|λ|K/3)=λ²/(2(1-|λ|K/3)).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-valued measurable random variable X on an arbitrary probability space, if X is integrable, centered, and satisfies |X|≤K almost surely for some positive K, then for every real λ with |λ|K<3, the exponential e^{λX} is integrable and its expectation is at most exp((λ²/(2(1-|λ|K/3)))·E[X²]).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The bound |X|≤K is only almost everywhere, not at every point of Ω.
The result applies only when K is strictly positive and |λ|K<3; equality |λ|K=3 and larger values are excluded.
The denominator 1-|λ|K/3 is positive under the stated λ restriction, so the displayed quotient does not encounter division by zero in admissible cases.
No independence, identical-distribution, symmetry, or finite/discrete sample-space assumption is present.
The proposition explicitly assumes both measurability and integrability of X, even though integrability itself includes almost-everywhere strong measurability.

The conclusion does not separately state that X² is integrable, although the probability-measure and almost-sure boundedness hypotheses mathematically ensure its integrability; syntactically, the Bochner integral ∫X²dμ is defined regardless.

The quantified implication is vacuous whenever any prerequisite fails, including absence of the required probability-measure instance, nonpositive K, failure of centering or boundedness, or a λ outside the strict domain.
The theorem does not assert that K is the smallest essential bound, only that it is some positive almost-sure bound.
